title: My Musings On The Iron Claw

commenti.body:
I think the film needed an extra 30min at least, maybe even an hour. The fact they cut out one sibling’s existence is just weird to me. But, more importantly, I think they needed more time to adequately capture the highs and lows the family experienced.

The first 40min were a real rush to experience, but once the tragedy comes I didn’t feel the weight I feel I was supposed too… it was just a little rushed, perhaps unsurprisingly, given the depth of loss the family experienced in a relatively short span of time. But if you’re going to approach a history like that, should probably give it the attention it calls for.

I think a documentary could maybe pull this off in 2hr, but for something more dramatic, we need more time to really feel the layered yet fracturing psychologies of the characters as events pile upon each other.

Durkin said it felt too repetitive to have three brothers commit suicide in succession (Chris killed himself between Mike and Kerry) which makes sense when it’s rushed already. You would miss out on a lot of characterisation for everyone else. I still agree it should’ve gone for added length to tell it more fairly, and you could use that time to include Chris without anyone else losing out.

Literally just finished the film. Was thinking the exact same, this could have been one of my favourites of the last 10 years if it was just more in depth. Very rarely this happens but I wish the film was 30 minutes or more longer.

i think because the film mostly happens through kevin’s pov, i’m okay with not elaborating on everyone in such a large way. i think a smaller, easier fix to the film is giving us even more interiority, so we could be inside kevin’s head. that way, you can have things happen quickly, and it becomes more about kevin reacting to them. i still really enjoyed the film though and think it deserves praise.

It would have worked better as a mini-series, and considering the popularity of the mini-series these days I'm surprised they didn't go that route.

There was so much exposition and awkward sounding conversation to provide history for the viewer that it made it difficult to really connect with the characters or understand what they were going through on a deeper level.

I get why they didn't throw in another half hour, it's already a long movie.  But I think it could have been great with another hour or maybe even 2, to really flesh everyone out.  As it is, I think it was fine, I didn't hate it, but it wasn't what I was hoping for.
